title: THE ADMIRALTY (JURISDICTION AND SETTLEMENT OF MARITIME CLAIMS) ACT, 2017
long_title: An Act to consolidate the laws relating to admiralty jurisdiction, legal proceedings in connection with vessels, their arrest, detention, sale and other matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.

sections.text: (1) This Act may be called the Admiralty (Jurisdiction and Settlement of Maritime Claims) Act, 2017. (2) It applies to every vessel, irrespective of the owner's residence or domicile, except an inland vessel under the Inland Vessels Act, 1917 or an unlaunched vessel under construction (unless notified), and does not apply to a warship, naval auxiliary or other government vessel used for non-commercial purposes, nor to a notified foreign non-commercial vessel. (3) It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification, appoint.

(1) Defines "admiralty jurisdiction", "admiralty proceeding", "arrest", "goods", "High Court" (listing the High Courts of Calcutta, Bombay, Madras, Karnataka, Gujarat, Orissa, Kerala, and Hyderabad for Telangana/Andhra Pradesh, or any other notified High Court), "maritime claim", "maritime lien", "notification", "port", "prescribed", "territorial waters", and "vessel" (including ships, boats, barges, hovercraft, offshore units, and sunk/stranded/abandoned vessels, but excluding a vessel broken up beyond use as certified by a surveyor). (2) Undefined terms used herein but defined in the Merchant Shipping Act, 1958 bear the meanings assigned there.

Subject to sections 4 and 5, admiralty jurisdiction over maritime claims vests in the respective High Courts over waters up to and including their territorial waters, extendable by the Central Government up to the limits under the Territorial Waters, Continental Shelf, Exclusive Economic Zone and Other Maritime Zones Act, 1976.

(1) Lists the categories of maritime claim over which the High Court may exercise jurisdiction against a vessel, including disputes over possession/ownership, co-owner disputes, mortgages/charges, loss or damage from vessel operation, loss of life or personal injury, loss of or damage to goods, carriage agreements, use/hire agreements, salvage, towage, pilotage, supplies and services to the vessel, construction/repair, port dues, crew wages, disbursements, average claims, sale disputes, insurance premiums, commission/brokerage/agency fees, environmental damage, wreck removal costs, and maritime liens. (2) The High Court may settle outstanding accounts between parties and order sale of the vessel or other relief. (3) On ordering sale, the High Court may determine title to the proceeds. (4) An arrested vessel or its sale proceeds are held as security pending final outcome.

(1) The High Court may order arrest of a vessel within its jurisdiction to secure a maritime claim, where it has reason to believe the owner or demise charterer liable for the claim remains owner/charterer at arrest, the claim is based on a mortgage/charge, relates to ownership/possession, or is secured by a maritime lien under section 9. (2) The High Court may order arrest of a sister vessel in lieu of the vessel concerned, except for claims under section 4(1)(a).
Subject to section 7, the High Court may exercise admiralty jurisdiction in personam in respect of maritime claims under section 4(1).

sections.section_title: Restrictions on actions in personam in certain cases
sections.text: (1) For claims arising from collision, manoeuvre, or non-compliance with collision regulations, the High Court shall not entertain an action unless the cause of action arose wholly or partly in India, or the defendant resides/works/does business in India, subject to a proviso for multiple defendants. (2) The High Court shall not entertain such an action until prior foreign proceedings on the same incident have ended. (3)-(4) Extends these rules to counter-claims. (5) These restrictions do not apply if the defendant submits to jurisdiction. (6) The High Court has jurisdiction whenever either condition in sub-section (1) is satisfied, and service-of-process laws apply.

sections.section_title: Vesting of rights on sale of vessels
sections.text: On a court sale, the vessel vests in the purchaser free of all encumbrances, liens, attachments, mortgages and charges.

sections.section_title: Inter se priority on maritime lien
sections.text: (1) Sets out the priority order of maritime liens: crew wages, loss of life/personal injury, salvage reward, port/canal/waterway dues, and tort claims from vessel operation (excluding cargo damage). (2) A maritime lien continues despite change of ownership, registration or flag, and is extinguished after one year (two years for wage claims) unless the vessel is arrested/seized leading to a forced sale. (3) Specifies when each lien period commences, excluding periods under arrest/seizure. (4) No maritime lien attaches for claims arising from oil/hazardous substance carriage compensable under other law, or from radioactive properties of nuclear fuel/waste.

sections.section_title: Order of priority of maritime claims
sections.text: (1) Priority order: claims with a maritime lien, then registered mortgages/charges, then all other claims. (2) Claims within the same priority category rank equally; salvage claims rank in inverse order of accrual.

sections.section_title: Protection of owner, demise charterer, manager or operator or crew of vessel arrested
sections.text: (1) The High Court may condition an arrest on the claimant giving an undertaking or security for damages arising from wrongful/unjustified arrest or excessive security demanded. (2) The security provider may apply to have the security reduced, modified or cancelled. (3) If the owner/charterer abandons the vessel after arrest, the High Court shall have it auctioned and proceeds dealt with within forty-five days (extendable by thirty days for recorded reasons).

sections.section_title: Application of Code of Civil Procedure
sections.text: The Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 applies to proceedings before the High Court insofar as not inconsistent with this Act or its rules.
(1) The Central Government shall notify a list of qualified assessors, their duties and fees, as prescribed. (2) Appointment of assessors does not bar examination of expert witnesses by parties.
An appeal lies from any judgment, decree, or final or interim order of a single Judge to a Division Bench of the High Court.

sections.section_title: Transfer of proceedings by Supreme Court
sections.text: The Supreme Court may, on application, transfer an admiralty proceeding between High Courts at any stage, after giving parties an opportunity to be heard; the transferee court continues from the stage of transfer.

(1) The Central Government may make rules to carry out the purposes of this Act. (2) Such rules may cover assessors' qualifications, duties and fees; practice and procedure of admiralty jurisdiction including fees and costs; and other prescribed matters. (3) Until Central Government rules are made, existing High Court rules governing admiralty jurisdiction continue to apply. (4) Every rule shall be laid before both Houses of Parliament for thirty days, subject to modification or annulment, without prejudice to things already done.

(1) Repeals the application in India of the Admiralty Court Act, 1840; the Admiralty Court Act, 1861; the Colonial Courts of Admiralty Act, 1890; the Colonial Courts of Admiralty (India) Act, 1891; and the admiralty-jurisdiction provisions of the Letters Patent, 1865 for the Bombay, Calcutta and Madras High Courts. (2) Pending admiralty proceedings continue to be adjudicated under this Act. (3)-(4) Actions, rules, and orders under the repealed enactments continue as if made under corresponding provisions of this Act, until superseded.

(1) The Central Government may, within three years of commencement, make orders not inconsistent with this Act to remove difficulties in giving effect to it. (2) Every such order shall be laid before both Houses of Parliament.
